title: The lucky prize
setting: A Saturday afternoon on the shopping street near their flat. Kenta and Sora have each just had a go at the shops' prize draw, and the sky is clouding over.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yatta! sora, mite! hon ga atatta!
lines.ja: やった！ソラ、見て！本が当たった！
lines.kana: やった！そら、みて！ほんがあたった！
lines.english: Yes! Sora, look! I won a book!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, honto ni? un ii ne!
lines.kana: え、ほんとに？うんいいね！

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ryouri no hon. kore, yuki no uchi de chotto yonda kedo, kekkou tame ni naru n da yo.
lines.ja: 料理の本。これ、ユキのうちでちょっと読んだけど、けっこうためになるんだよ。
lines.kana: りょうりのほん。これ、ゆきのうちでちょっとよんだけど、けっこうためになるんだよ。
lines.english: A cookbook. I read a bit of it at Yuki's place, and it's actually pretty worthwhile.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ryouri no hon kaa. boku, ryouri shinai kara, yonde mo tame ni naranai naa.
lines.ja: 料理の本かあ。僕、料理しないから、読んでもためにならないなあ。
lines.kana: りょうりのほんかあ。ぼく、りょうりしないから、よんでもためにならないなあ。
lines.english: A cookbook, huh. I don't cook, so reading it wouldn't do me any good.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.kana: そらは？なにがあたった？
lines.english: What about you, Sora? What did you win?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kasa ka. demo, kasa wa yaku ni tatsu yo.
lines.ja: 傘か。でも、傘は役に立つよ。
lines.kana: かさか。でも、かさはやくにたつよ。
lines.english: An umbrella, huh. Well, umbrellas are useful.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yaku ni wa tatsu kedo, uchi ni mou itsutsu mo aru yo.
lines.ja: 役には立つけど、うちにもう五つもあるよ。
lines.kana: やくにはたつけど、うちにもういつつもあるよ。
lines.english: Sure they're useful, but we've already got five at home.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: aa, sore wa un warukatta ne.
lines.ja: ああ、それは運悪かったね。
lines.kana: ああ、それはうんわるかったね。

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: kenta wa un ii yo ne. boku wa honto ni un warui naa.
lines.ja: ケンタは運いいよね。僕はほんとに運悪いなあ。
lines.kana: けんたはうんいいよね。ぼくはほんとにうんわるいなあ。
lines.english: You're the lucky one, Kenta. I'm just so unlucky.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: a, ame futte kita! hon ga dame ni natchau!
lines.ja: あ、雨降ってきた！本がダメになっちゃう！
lines.kana: あ、あめふってきた！ほんがだめになっちゃう！
lines.english: Oh no, it's started raining! The book's going to get ruined!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: daijoubu! kasa sasu kara, kenta mo haitte.
lines.ja: 大丈夫！傘さすから、ケンタも入って。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ！かささすから、けんたもはいって。
lines.english: It's okay! I'll put the umbrella up. Get under it too, Kenta.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: arigatou! sora no kasa, metcha yaku ni tatta ne.
lines.ja: ありがとう！ソラの傘、めっちゃ役に立ったね。
lines.kana: ありがとう！そらのかさ、めっちゃやくにたったね。
lines.english: Thanks! Your umbrella really came in handy.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, honto ni un ga ii no wa boku da ne!
lines.ja: じゃあ、ほんとに運がいいのは僕だね！
lines.kana: じゃあ、ほんとにうんがいいのはぼくだね！
lines.english: So I'm the one who's really lucky!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. kyou wa kono hon mite, sora ni ryouri tsukuru yo.
lines.ja: うん。今日はこの本見て、ソラに料理作るよ。
lines.kana: うん。きょうはこのほんみて、そらにりょうりつくるよ。
lines.english: Yeah. Today I'll cook you something out of this book.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: yatta! sono hon, boku no tame ni mo naru ne!
lines.ja: やった！その本、僕のためにもなるね！
lines.kana: やった！そのほん、ぼくのためにもなるね！
lines.english: Yay! So that book does me some good too!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: あはは。じゃあ、うちに帰ろう。
lines.kana: あはは。じゃあ、うちにかえろう。
lines.english: Ha ha. Okay, let's get home.

choices.english: The rain ruins Kenta's new cookbook, so Sora cheers him up by offering to cook dinner.
Sora is disappointed to win only an umbrella, but it keeps Kenta's new book dry in the rain, and Kenta says he'll cook for him.
Sora wins a cookbook he has no use for, so he swaps it with Kenta for an umbrella.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Kenta wins a book in the draw, and line 3 says it's a cookbook. Sora only wins an umbrella (lines 5-6), and they already have five at home (line 8), so he feels unlucky (line 10: boku wa honto ni un warui naa). Then it starts raining and Kenta is worried the book will be ruined (line 11). Sora puts up his umbrella and Kenta gets under it (lines 12-13). Sora decides he's the lucky one after all (line 14), and Kenta says he'll cook for him from the book (line 15). A is wrong: the book never gets ruined, because the umbrella keeps it dry. Sora also doesn't cook (line 4: ryouri shinai). C is wrong: Kenta won the cookbook and Sora won the umbrella, and nobody swaps prizes.

questions.english: Yuki's little brother Kenji tells you how his exam went: "kyou shiken datta n da kedo, kinou benkyou shita no ga deta n da." (I had an exam today, and the stuff I studied yesterday came up.) Tell him he was lucky.
questions.ja: 今日試験だったんだけど、昨日勉強したのが出たんだ。
questions.kana: きょうしけんだったんだけど、きのうべんきょうしたのがでたんだ。
questions.romaji: kyou shiken datta n da kedo, kinou benkyou shita no ga deta n da.
questions.answer: Tell him he was lucky with luck as the subject: un ii ne! (ga dropped). Or, since it's already happened, use the past: un ga yokatta ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: sore wa un ga yokatta ne.
modelAnswers.ja: それは運がよかったね。

questions.explanation: Sora says the first answer to Kenta in line 2 (e, honto ni? un ii ne!) when Kenta wins the book. In line 14 he keeps ga: honto ni un ga ii no wa boku da ne. In Japanese the luck is the subject (un ga ii: the luck is good), so you don't put 'lucky' on the person the way English does. The past of ii is yokatta, so 'that was lucky' is un ga yokatta, never un iikatta. 'Good luck!' before an exam is ganbatte and has nothing to do with un. Here the exam is already over, so you're commenting on luck that has already happened.

questions.english: Sora shows Kenta the umbrella he won and says they already have five at home. Kenta says "aa, sore wa un warukatta ne." What does Kenta mean?
questions.ja: 運悪かったねって、何ですか？
questions.kana: うんわるかったねって、なんですか？
questions.romaji: un warukatta ne tte, nan desu ka?

choices.english: That was a bad choice. Sora should have gone for a different prize.
That's a bad umbrella. It probably won't last in the rain.
That was just bad luck. It's nobody's fault he got another umbrella.

questions.explanation: Line 9: un warukatta ne is the usual way to console someone. The luck was bad (warukatta is the past of warui), and ga is dropped. On its own, warui can mean poor quality or at fault, but with un it is only about luck. A is wrong: prizes are won in a draw, not chosen (atatta, lines 1 and 5), and Kenta isn't blaming Sora. B is wrong: Kenta says nothing against the umbrella, and it works fine when the rain comes (lines 12-13). Sora answers in line 10 with both phrases in one frame: kenta wa un ii yo ne. boku wa honto ni un warui naa.

questions.english: When the rain starts and Sora puts up his umbrella, Kenta thanks him. What did Kenta say about the umbrella?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: けんたさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Your umbrella really came in handy.
choices.romaji: sora no kasa, metcha yaku ni tatta ne.
sora no kasa, metcha benri datta ne.

choices.english: Your umbrella really did me good.
choices.romaji: sora no kasa, metcha tame ni natta ne.

questions.explanation: Line 13: yaku ni tatta, the past of yaku ni tatsu, says the umbrella actually helped: it kept Kenta's new book out of the rain. B is what you get by translating the English word 'useful' as benri. Benri means handy or convenient to use, like a shop close to home. It describes how easy something is to use, not that it just got you out of trouble. C is the chunk's other phrase, tame ni naru. That one is for a book, a talk or a show that does you good over time, the way Kenta describes the cookbook in line 3. An umbrella can help you, but it doesn't teach you anything. Lines 3 and 7 already set the two apart: the book is tame ni naru, and the umbrella is yaku ni tatsu.

questions.english: Yuki sees the book you're carrying and asks, "sono hon, mou yonda? ii hon?" (Have you read that book yet? Is it any good?) Tell her it's really worthwhile.
questions.ja: その本、もう読んだ？いい本？
questions.kana: そのほん、もうよんだ？いいほん？
questions.romaji: sono hon, mou yonda? ii hon?
questions.answer: Say it's worth reading with tame ni naru, keeping ni: un, sugoku tame ni naru yo. Before a noun it becomes tame ni naru hon.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, sugoku tame ni naru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、すごくためになるよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: un, kekkou tame ni naru hon da yo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、けっこうためになる本だよ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, it's a pretty worthwhile book.

questions.explanation: Kenta says the same thing about the cookbook in line 3 (kekkou tame ni naru n da yo). Sora turns it round in line 4 (yonde mo tame ni naranai naa) and again in line 16 (boku no tame ni mo naru ne). Tame ni naru says a book, show or talk is good for you, something you come away from knowing more. Yaku ni tatsu is practical help with a task, like the umbrella in line 13. Ni stays even in casual speech. This is not the grammar -tame ni (in order to): here tame means benefit, and the phrase ends in naru.

newWords.english: cooking; a dish (ryouri no hon = a cookbook; ryouri suru = to cook)
to be won in a draw (hon ga atatta = I won a book; nani ga atatta? = what did you win?)
to make, to cook (ryouri tsukuru = cook a meal)
